page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-hypervisor instance equipped with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the platform features 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. Storage is handled locally by 5,700 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Acceleration hardware such as GPUs is absent on this model.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier and strong throughput in heavily multi-threaded workloads, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,800, strong stress-ng multi-core execution (92,851.92), and leading PassMark CPU encryption performance. Memory throughput is solid, maintaining 328.42 GB/sec read and 139.93 GB/sec write bandwidth on large data blocks. While single-threaded performance remains in the average band across Geekbench and compression tasks, distributed operations such as Redis SET achieve 89.82 million operations per second, supported by 66.38 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the instance stems from its CPU-only inference limitations on large-scale deep learning models, exhibiting weak 70B parameter LLM token generation rates alongside average single-core speed. However, dense local NVMe storage combined with high baseline networking provides strong cost efficiency for I/O-intensive services without requiring detached EBS volumes. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for enterprise database clusters, distributed caching tiers, in-memory data processing, high-traffic web serving, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and 384 GB of DDR4 RAM, it offers a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio alongside 5,700 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 150 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded compute, superior cryptographic performance, and high memory bandwidth, achieving 89.82 million Redis SET operations per second and 66.38 GB/sec web serving throughput. Single-core processing and large-parameter LLM inference remain average or lower, presenting clear architectural boundaries. With its dense core count, high-speed local disk, and massive network capacity, this server is suitable for enterprise databases, distributed caching layers, large CI/CD build farms, and memory-intensive web workloads.
